name: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Cut chicken into bite-sized cubes. Marinate with soy sauce and cornstarch.
Mix sauce: soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and cornstarch.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns for 30 seconds.
Add marinated chicken and cook until golden.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in sauce mixture and toss to coat.
Add peanuts and green onions, toss and serve immediately.
cooking_tips: High heat is essential for proper wok cooking.
Have all ingredients prepped before starting — it cooks fast.
Toast peanuts beforehand for better flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve over steamed white rice or fried rice.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Best eaten fresh.

name: Egg Fried Rice
instructions: Use day-old cold rice for best results.
Beat eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Scramble eggs in the wok, break into small pieces, set aside.
Add more oil, stir-fry garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add cold rice and stir-fry vigorously, breaking up any clumps.
Add scrambled eggs back and toss together.
Season with soy sauce, white pepper, and sesame oil. Top with green onions.
cooking_tips: Cold, day-old rice is key — fresh rice gets mushy.
Cook on very high heat for the 'wok hei' smoky flavor.
Keep everything moving in the wok.
serving_suggestions: Serve as a main dish or as a side with other Chinese dishes.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot wok.

name: Sweet and Sour Pork
instructions: Cut pork into chunks, marinate with soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Coat pork pieces in egg then cornstarch.
Deep fry pork until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Make sauce: mix ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and water.
Stir-fry onions, bell peppers, and pineapple for 2 minutes.
Add sauce and bring to a boil.
Add fried pork and toss to coat.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry if needed.
cooking_tips: Double frying pork makes it extra crispy.
Add pork at the last minute to keep it crispy.
Fresh pineapple gives better flavor than canned.
serving_suggestions: Serve over steamed rice with a garnish of sesame seeds.
storage_tips: Store sauce and pork separately. Combine when serving.

substitutions.ketchup: tomato paste with extra vinegar and sugar

name: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Cut tofu into 1-inch cubes. Blanch in salted water for 2 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok, fry garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add chili bean paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add vegetable broth and bring to simmer.
Gently add tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry.
Garnish with Sichuan pepper and green onions.
cooking_tips: Silken tofu is traditional but firm tofu holds up better.
Sichuan peppercorns give the characteristic numbing sensation.
serving_suggestions: Serve over steamed rice. The spicy sauce is perfect for soaking up.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days but tofu softens over time.

name: Spring Rolls
instructions: Shred cabbage and carrots, slice mushrooms thin.
Stir-fry vegetables with garlic and ginger until softened.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil. Let cool completely.
Place filling on spring roll wrapper diagonally.
Fold in sides, roll tightly, seal edge with cornstarch paste.
Heat oil to 175°C for deep frying.
Fry spring rolls in batches until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Let filling cool completely before rolling to prevent soggy wrappers.
Make sure oil is hot enough before frying.
For baked version, brush with oil and bake at 200°C.
serving_suggestions: Serve with sweet chili sauce or soy dipping sauce.
storage_tips: Freeze uncooked rolls for up to 2 months. Fry from frozen.
